title: Fomo Kernel Condition Check
description: One per-period check of a condition slot (#412): whether new information arrived this review period, and — for a numeric slot — whether the threshold was crossed. The readable contract; skills/fomo-kernel/engine/conditions.py (build_check) holds the enforcement, because the offline suite carries no jsonschema dependency. Two shapes appear here: `input` is what an agent may put on the check envelope; the rest of the document is the durable row stored in <root>/condition_checks.jsonl — a separate append-only file from conditions.jsonl. Check rows are an event stream and slot rows are identity; the two row shapes are never mixed in one file.

check_id.description: Engine-assigned identity for this check row.

slot_id.description: The concrete slot row this check evaluated — not the line id. A check always names exactly the slot version it looked at; previous_check_for resolves history across a revision by walking the slot's line.

session_id.description: The session that recorded this check, or null when none was given.

date_end.description: The review period end this check belongs to.

lookup_status.description: ok: an observation was found and is attached. failed: a lookup was attempted and did not produce a usable observation. not_checked: no lookup was attempted this period.

reason.description: Free text explaining a failed or not_checked lookup_status.

observation.description: This period's evidence. Present only when lookup_status is ok; forbidden otherwise.

information_state.description: Whether this observation is new information, identified by (effective_period, document, value-or-summary) against the previous ok-check's observation, or — absent one — the slot's baseline. null unless lookup_status is ok: there is nothing to classify without a fresh observation.

engine_verdict.description: The engine's own comparison for a numeric slot, computed from the slot's frozen threshold and near_line against this observation — never overwritten by a later user override. Always null for an event slot: the engine never computes an event verdict. Also null for any slot whenever lookup_status is not ok, because there is no fresh observation to evaluate.

final_verdict.description: The verdict of record. For a numeric slot with no user_response this equals engine_verdict (or unknown when the lookup did not succeed); confirmed keeps engine_verdict under verdict_source user; overridden always becomes not_met. For an event slot this is unknown until the user answers yes (met) or no (not_met) — store, never infer.

verdict_source.description: Whether final_verdict came from the engine's own comparison or from the user's response on this check.

user_response.description: The user's response to this check, when one was given.

created.description: Matches date_end — the same 'created' convention every other row in this store's family uses.

input.description: What an agent may place on the check envelope. Everything else in this document is engine-assigned; supplying it is an error.

observation.description: One evidence record for this check. Exactly one of value (numeric slot) or summary (event slot) must be present — never both, never neither; conditions.py fails closed on the mismatch.

as_of.description: The date the figure or fact describes, not the date it was read.

period.description: Period identity (fiscal quarter, month). Half of what identifies new information from a re-worded same-period result.

document.description: Document identity (filing, release). The other half.

user_response.description: The user's reaction to this check. answer's vocabulary depends on the slot's kind: confirmed/overridden for numeric, yes/no for event — conditions.py fails closed on the wrong kind's vocabulary.
